The same Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria, provides a few fragments on the second epistle to the Corinthians. Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy, the brother, are introduced. The wisest apostle Paul, having been entrusted with the ministry concerning Christ by the will of God, says that he is driven to speak against the false prophets and false apostles as impious, speaking in the Spirit and having Jesus Christ strengthened within his own soul. He claims to have the Spirit of God and to be a servant of Christ, although God is the ruler of all. It is said to him that all things are his servants, and thus he clearly attributes divine and true lordship to Christ. He calls himself an apostle of Jesus Christ, and thus proclaims Jesus Christ as God by nature and truth. For no one would be an apostle of men, but rather of God, according to nature. He shows that he was not called to apostleship by the opinion of the Father, nor does he speak from his heart like the false prophets, but rather serves the words of God. He makes Timothy a partner in the epistle, as one who is approved and follows in his footsteps, so that he may persuade more strongly through their agreement, since the law says that every word will be established on the testimony of two or three witnesses. This is addressed to the church of God which is in Corinth.

pass_b_english: The same Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria, provides a few fragments on the second epistle to the Corinthians. Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy, the brother, are introduced.

Paul, the wisest apostle, having been entrusted with the ministry concerning Christ by the will of God, speaks against the false prophets and false apostles as impious, driven by the Spirit and having Jesus Christ strengthened within his own soul.
He claims to have the Spirit of God and to be a servant of Christ, although God is the ruler of all.
He says, "I think that I too have the Spirit of God", and "If you seek proof of Christ speaking in me."
As it is said to him, all things are his servants, and thus he clearly attributes divine and true lordship to Christ.
He calls himself an apostle of Jesus Christ, proclaiming Jesus Christ as God by nature and truth.

He makes Timothy a partner in the epistle, as one who is approved and follows in his footsteps, so that he may persuade more strongly through their agreement, since the law says that every word will be established on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
This is addressed to the church of God which is in Corinth.
The church of God in Corinth, which is also called Christ's church, is the recipient of this letter.
Christ himself presented the church to himself as a pure and virgin bride.
If the church belongs to God and Christ has presented it to himself, then it is clear that God is the one who has come from the holy and God-bearing Mary.
We greet you with the grace and peace that come from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ.
If someone did not consider the Son to be God by nature, it would be more appropriate to say that grace and peace come from God the Father alone.
However, by receiving Christ as a co-giver of divine gifts, it is evident that the Son is indeed God by nature.
This is why we must receive the Son along with the Father in our discussion of unity and co-essence, so that we may understand God as the sole giver of spiritual goods.
Christ Jesus is the Word of God who has been manifested in the flesh, and if he gives the same things as the Father, then he must be considered God by nature through his union with his own flesh.
As the apostle Paul says, Christ is God over all, blessed forever.
We are confident that our word to you is not a mixture of yes and no, for God is faithful.
No one can say that Jesus is Lord except in the Holy Spirit, and the Spirit is truth, as it is written.
The preachers of the evangelical decrees, being filled with the truth of the Holy Spirit, would not be considered false speakers, for they speak with a mind guided by the Spirit.
Whatever they say about Christ is right and unshakeable, firmly grounded in the truth.
Christ himself affirms this, saying that it is not the speakers themselves who speak, but the Spirit of their Father speaking through them.
This is not to say that he speaks contradictory things, now preaching Jesus as God by nature, and now as a man.
Rather, he yields to the unreasonableness of those who accuse him of contradiction, and his words are not double or divided.

καίτοι τῶν ὅλων κατεξουσιάζοντος τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ κατάρχοντος μόνου· εἴρηται γὰρ πρὸς
αὐτόν " Οτι τὰ σύμπαντα δοῦλα σά·" πῶς οὖν οὐκ ἐναργῶς φυσικήν τε αὐτῷ καὶ ἀληθῶς
θεοπρεπεστάτην τῆς κυριότητος ἀπονέμει δόξαν; 321 Ἐξ ὧν ἀπόστολον ἑαυτὸν λέγει
τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Θεὸν φύσει καὶ ἀληθῶς καταγγέλλει τὸν Ἰησοῦν· οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἀπόστολον εἴη
ἂν ἀνθρώπων ἀλλὰ Θεοῦ μᾶλλον τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν· καὶ δείκνυσιν ὅτι οὐ παρὰ γνώμην

τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ, καίτοι Χριστοῦ λεγομένης εἶναι τῆς Ἐκκλησίας· αὐτὸς γὰρ αὐτὴν
ἑαυτῷ παρέστησε παρθένον ἁγνήν· εἴπερ οὖν ἐστιν ἡ Ἐκκλησία Θεοῦ, Χριστὸς δὲ ὁ
ταύτην ἑαυτῷ παραστήσας, Θεὸς ἄρα κατὰ φύσιν ἐστὶν ὁ ἐκ τῆς ἁγίας καὶ θεοτόκου
Μαρίας. Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Εἴπερ
οὐκ ὄντα Θεὸν κατὰ φύσιν ἠπίστατο τὸν Υἱὸν, πῶς οὐκ ἔδει μᾶλλον εἰπεῖν Χάρις ὑμῖν
καὶ εἰρήνη παρὰ μόνου τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός; νυνὶ δὲ συνεισδεχόμενος καὶ συνδοτῆρα
τιθεὶς τὸν Χριστὸν ὧν ἂν ἡ θεία χαρίσαιτο φύσις, δῆλος ἂν εἴη δήπουθεν οὐκ ἠγνοηκὼς

Υἱὸν εἰς τὸν τῆς ταυτότητός τε καὶ ὁμοουσιότητος λόγον, ἵνα καὶ Θεὸς εἷς χορηγὸς
